newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares supported by ADR demand, seen up.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares supported by ADR demand, seen up.

text.p: Russian regional energy company Mosenergo lent support to Russian shares early Friday, and follow-through buying from Thursday's record close could push them to a fresh high Friday, traders said.
"I think we'll see a new (Russian Trading System) record (today) based on buying from yesterday," said Brunswick trader Gary Kinsey.
The RTS index of 22 leading shares opened slightly off at 388.54 from 388.99 at the close on Thursday.
"All the 'blue chips' are in demand," Kinsey said. "(Mosenergo) hasn't really moved for a while and new money coming into market is looking especially at Mosenergo."

Rossiisky Kredit Bank trader Oleg Martynenko said a good credit rating and a 56 percent jump in 1996 net profits posted on Monday had made Mosenergo a bargain, helping to boost the stock in the last few days.
But a correction lower was now possible, he said.
"After the close (on Thursday) there were buys on Mosenergo but after such a sharp growth there is always a falling back," Martynenko said.
Mosenergo rose to $1.427 at 0905 GMT after closing on Thursday at $1.414. National power company UES also edged up to $0.3275 from $0.3270. Oil company LUKoil slipped to $17.20 after $17.25.
Brunswick's Kinsey said demand for American Depositary Reciepts on leading Russian shares from foreign investment funds was pulling underlying local share prices higher.

"The price of ADRs (American Depositary Receipts) ended higher (in New York) than prices here -- that's been the theme for the week," Kinsey said. "Blue chip demand is higher in ADRs than in Moscow and it has driven prices higher here."
National savings bank Sberbank hit $300.00 after closing at $296.00 on Thursday.

Kinsey said Western fund managers were putting money into Russian shares based on movement on a key tax reform bill and progress in untangling a web of non-payments between companies and the government.
"People really believe the tax situation will be sorted out and there seems to be a conviction that the complexity of the non-payments crisis will be sorted out," he said.
But he said growth next week would depend on how new investors, who he said had so far been prepared to pay up for stock, reacted to the new levels on Friday.
